reviews.review_description: We had 40 kw system installed designed to cover our electricity usage.  Rang Zen several times to tell them it didn’t seem to be working properly.  Told to check monitor every time.  Electrician called in one day to check.  Monitor is okay.  Last week independent technician came to check the whole system.  Apart from microinverter, just one, fused everything appeared okay.  Except the wiring was all wrong.  The power generated was wired to go straight back into the grid.  8 years of high energy bills.  We never had the use of solar generated power so bills stayed high.  Zen have no interest in knowing or doing anything about it.  Still in shock.  All that money for solar system and high energy bills as well.  No support from Zen.  Astounding.
Sales and quoting process was very handled, all questions answered promptly. Installation was prompt and done well. Customer service was very good.

What has happened to Zen service ?   we have accepted their quote, now cant get hold of someone who will tell us accurately when and if its accepted and when installation will happen,, we have installed Zen panels 7 years previously and the service advise etc was exceptional then, but now they have become a mega company the residential installs dont seem to matter,,,

reviews.review_description: From the very beginning contact with Zen Energy through to quoting and then to installation. The whole process was smooth, and happened pretty quickly too. The team at Zen Energy were very informative, answered my many, many questions, and were very helpful. We nutted down to what I was happy with design wise, and product selection too. Got our approval in no time and installation was done within 2 weeks. Very happy with that. The installation team were awesome with their professionalism and safety. The whole day went smoothly and they did a fantastic job. Cleaning up after themselves too. I was informed throughout the day what steps they were up to. And then had the ins and outs of the inverter explained to me as well as wifi connection setup. A great job, and very happy. Thanks Zen Energy.

Getting numerous quotes and referrals is a good way to do business with solar supply and installation.  The quotation process gives an opportunity for the buyer to learn the facts, the jargon and the intricacies of solar energy.  The more quotes you get the more you learn and understand about the systems.  Do not be price-driven during this phase, it should always be about quality, installation, workmanship, warranty and after-sales service.  Choose a company that you think will likely be operating decades into the future.  Look at the company closely, its management structure, its track-record, where it is located, who owns it and what are their strategic plans and long-term goals.  In short, don't deal with cowboys who try and up-sell their products and seek to install a system that is larger than your needs and cheaper than everyone else. Buy the very best inverter on the market and do your homework on the PV panels, their performance is extremely variable.

Several years ago we installed ZENs 3kW system (and solar hot water system) and we were very happy with what we have got then. ZEN was more expensive than others but - and though it was not necessary offering better/the best quality system components, we liked how ZEN looked at that time. Its installations were aesthetically superior (tidy, all black, with hidden brackets and black capped rail ends), and their business/company was well presented too... We now wanted "extension". But did not ask necessary questions. We trusted the BRAND. We have got an ordinary 1.5kW  "industrial" and separated system/"extension". And extraordinary extended delays. Job first delayed and at the present time still not completed (several weeks later)... If somebody would ask me I think that ZEN doesn't exists anymore. Somebody just uses ZEN brand name to sell what any other "solar business" could sell to you - ET Solar panels, Enphase Micro Inverters,  and "standard" mounting system. As in our example... If you are still tempted get quote from ZEN (or so called) Energy and then talk to you "local installers". Unless you cannot get a better price from ZEN (for the same product), in my opinion you have no reason to go with them...

Zen supplied our original system in 2010 and we were very happy with the service and quality of the system so we decided to try them again.One disadvantage of this company now is they do not have a shop front locally only a representative who is sometime difficult to contact.We are promised a free net meter from Origin Energy sometime soon but I can see problems ahead coordinating Zen and Origin Energy so we can have the system working by late Oct 2016.

Due to be installed 16 September.  Communication from Zen has been very good to date.Post Install Update:I thought you might like some more up-to-date feedback on my solar installation.Our solar panels etc were installed on 16 September by Zen Home Energy Systems.  We are expecting ETSA Utilities to change over our 3 phase analogue meter on 1 November.  It seems that Zen did not reqest ETSA to do this until they had installed the panels, even though we ordered the system about 3 months earlier.  Fortunately, our meter runs backwards when the sun is generating enough power, but clearly ETSA has no motivation to rush the meter changeover!Our portable meter, which monitors the power generated by the panels, rarely matches the reading on the inverter box, due (according to Zen's Technical Manager) to the vagaries of the bluetooth device.  The daily graph also varies quite a lot - so the result is that I am unsure of what is actually being generated.  Zen has been reluctant to do anything about this so far, but I will persist.  The portable device also had a progamming fault which they corrected, but only after several weeks from my being first told about it when I complained about the device's odd results.  The results still seem odd, even after the fix.
Overall I was happy with the service your site provided. It certainly made my decision more informed than it would have otherwise been and gave me the confidence to proceed with solar power.
Still in process.  Let me get back to you after installation and an initial month or so of operations.

It really came down to between ZEN and SolarSA for us, both companies seemed to be very professional, and gave great detail in operation etc of their products.

Our solar array was installed professionally with a very high attention to detail on March 3rd 2011. The problem is that the ETSA input/export install date was not to be until March 18th.(We were not informed of this date). I understand that ETSA are snowed under as well as Zen's contractors and that Zen were not aware of ETSA date until their contractors were booked in. But no effort to change our install date was made. Now, with much frustration (due to incredible sunny days), we have to wait fifteen days to turn on our array.Solar panels start to degrade on day one, so we are losing money(not much, but its the principle). I therefore have not been able to determine if it can perform to the appropriate level but we still have to pay up on the balance owing.
